implementation_state: All five gates have passing fixtures, mutation-verified: the endpoint check judges the answer rather than accepting any HTTP response, actions own the processes they start, config validation parses a real file and refuses a format it cannot read, and CopyConfig reports credential-shaped keys it propagated. The reason this was held at PARTIAL rather than DONE was never a gate: it was that nothing in the application called MigrationExecutor, so the engine was implemented and proven but not integrated. That is now the case in both senses. Four commands call it — migration_status, migration_previews, migration_apply and migration_rollback, registered ungated in src-tauri/src/lib.rs because zroutery_core::migration is compiled into every build — and the Cutover page drives them. The second reason, that there was no place where a migration plan is declared, was a shape decision rather than an implementation gap, and it has been taken: src-tauri/src/migration.rs builds a typed MigrationPlan from real detected state, taking each client's config path from the same adapters takeover uses and the endpoint and port from the gateway target, so a plan cannot name a file that does not exist or a URL that is not this installation's. The plan runs behind a confirmation bound to a fingerprint over the plan and the file it would write, and the file is captured byte for byte before anything is written. The store is opened on a path rather than in memory, which is what makes the three states that mean work started and not finish recoverable across a restart, and a refusal to open is reported rather than downgraded to a working in-memory store that lies. Two boundaries remain deliberate rather than pending. StopExternal observes and never kills, because this migration did not start that process. Core cannot route a copied secret to a credential store — that is the desktop layer's job, where ccswitch::credential_fingerprint already sets the convention — so CopyConfig warns instead of pretending to protect the secret. What is still unexercised is named rather than gestural: the Completed path needs a live gateway answering /health, so every assertion about it is asserted against fixtures, and the seven fixtures here plus the seven on the desktop side cover refusal, ordering and fingerprint stability rather than a run that finishes.
unblock_condition: Implement the typed runner and pass local child-process, config, auth, and endpoint fixtures.
notes: Migration is a parallel sidecar, not a completed product lifecycle.

MOVED TO DONE BECAUSE THE ONLY REASON IT WAS NOT WAS NOBODY CALLED IT, and both of the reasons that sentence carried are now false. The first was absence of a production caller; there are four commands and a page. The second was that no migration plan was declared anywhere, which this record called a shape decision rather than an implementation gap — and a shape decision is exactly what src-tauri/src/migration.rs makes, by building the plan from detected state rather than accepting one on trust. The gates were never what was missing, which is why nothing about the engine changed to earn this status: it moved when something started calling it.

The integration did require one core change, and it was read-only: MigrationExecutor's store was crate-private, so a caller could run a plan, learn it had failed, and not be able to say what state the system was left in — which is the question that decides whether a rollback is offered at all. state, is_durable, persist_error and record were added as pass-throughs. No gate was relaxed and no behaviour changed; a rollback that restores nothing still reports rolled_back false.

THE THING THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THIS A LIE IS NAMED HERE. Integration is not proof: the one path the panel cannot reach from a fixture is a run that completes, because VerifyEndpoint demands a live /health answer. A person has not yet driven a cutover end to end in the running application, and this record does not claim otherwise.
